react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolite set converges on two interconnected metabolic axes. The dominant signal is Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260), which achieves the highest cross-paradigm rank: RaMP multi-DB ORA reports FDR = 3.1e-16 (7 metabolites: choline, phosphoserine, sarcosine, AMP, SAM, lipoic acid, L-cystathionine), and mummichog m/z-direct analysis returns p = 0.022 with all 8 of its matched compounds falling within this pathway (perfect overlap). The pathway bridges one-carbon folate metabolism (via sarcosine and SAM) with trans-sulfuration (via L-cystathionine) and cofactor-dependent reactions (via lipoic acid and AMP as adenine nucleotide). The second axis, Glycerophospholipid metabolism, is supported by both mummichog (p = 0.039, rank 1: choline, cholesterol, phosphocholine) and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (hsa00564, p = 0.02, rank 3: phosphocholine + choline), indicating phospholipid membrane remodeling co-occurs with the amino-acid perturbation. Cysteine and methionine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270) is a significant secondary ORA hit (MetaboAnalystR p = 0.0009, rank 2; driver: SAM + L-cystathionine). Biotin metabolism (Mummichog rank 5, driver: biocytin) and pyrimidine metabolism (Mummichog rank 10, driver: UMP) appear as pathway-specific signals. The convergence of one-carbon metabolism, phospholipid dynamics, and nucleotide metabolism suggests a treatment-induced shift in both methyl-donor availability and cellular energy status.
